Page13 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 3 FACILITY SITING STUDY The primary requirement which Aptamus identified for the selection of a suitable site for T-RICH was that it be on, or near, a deep-water navigable shipping channel capable of accommodating vessels with a draft of at least 30 feet (9.1 meters). Being on such a channel will allow for the export of CO from the T-RICH 2 site via ocean going marine vessels. This supports Aptamus’ original vision of a marine transportation system to move CO captured at industrial sites in Florida to Louisiana and Texas for use in enhanced oil 2 recovery or for permanent sequestration since those states contain the nation’s largest confirmed safe underground CO storage sites. Since Aptamus and its affiliate company OSG are based in Tampa, Florida, 2 the Port of Tampa Bay (PTB) was contacted to identify vacant marine terminal sites that would facilitate the export of CO via marine vessels. Ideally the site would be next to an existing deepwater navigable 2 waterway or reasonably close enough to one that a short pipeline from the hub site to a marine berth could be installed. PTB has several such terminal sites available, but one stands out to both parties as being particularly appealing for the T-RICH site. The site is on the Pendola Point Peninsula, near existing Berth 30. Additional advantages include the fact that the site is surrounded by existing, active industrial terminal sites and is more than one mile from the nearest residential or public building and road. Several existing industrial facilities nearby already handle and process liquefied gases with similarities to liquified CO , so Pendola 2 Point contains existing hazardous materials facilities and has excellent rail and truck access. The proposed site is owned by Port Tampa Bay, located in the City of Tampa, Hillsborough County, FL. The red dot in Figure 3.1 depicts the site within the city and county. Hillsborough County includes the City of Tampa and large suburban municipalities such as Brandon, Riverview, and Town ‘n’ Country. The total county population is 1,451,358 people as of the last reported census.
